title: Aged well, or simply new once
subtitle: After eight years at sea, a ship's design has told you which of the two it is.

text: Good materials record use. Fashionable ones only deteriorate.
sub: Oak darkens, brass dulls, leather softens, wool wears in. Lacquer chips, chrome pits, backlit acrylic yellows, and the feature wall becomes a date stamp.

quote: A well-made room gets refreshed. A fashionable one has to be replaced — usually by whoever chose it wrongly the first time.

title: Three tells on any deck plan

items.head: The library, if there is one
items.body: A real library means the line believes in sea days. A shelf of decorative spines means it believes in photographs.

items.head: The number of screens
items.body: Digital signage on every landing dates faster than anything afloat, and makes a public room feel like an airport.

items.head: Whether you can move a chair
items.body: Fixed, bolted, arranged-for-the-camera seating tells you the room was designed to be looked at, not sat in.

text: Good bones beat a recent refit almost every time.
sub: A twenty-year-old ship built in oak and brass will be pleasant for another twenty. The sea is the view; the room only has to be quiet, well made, and not shouting its year.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: Then send me a ship you're considering and I'll give you two honest lines on whether it has aged or merely been refitted.
